summary: The note describes how Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality are being adopted in classrooms in underdeveloped regions to narrow educational gaps. It gives examples from Kenya, Peru, India, Ghana, Egypt and Colombia, with teacher testimonies and reports from late 2023. It also covers personalization of learning and the need for teacher training to overcome infrastructure and skills challenges.
one_line: VR and AR are being used in underserved classrooms worldwide, from Kenya to Colombia, to expand access, inclusivity and personalized learning.
key_facts: On September 20, 2023, a classroom in Nanyuki, Kenya, used AR to show students celestial bodies under the "Vision 2030" outreach initiative.
Catherine Mburu leads the AR project in the Nanyuki region and said the technology "has opened worlds."
The Global Education Monitoring Initiative published a report on October 8, 2023, on the role of immersive tech in delivering quality education to remote areas.
Peruvian educator Julio Torres uses AR in the Andean highlands to bring history lessons about the Incas to life.
A study dated September 15, 2023, by the Asia Pacific Technology for Education Consortium examined immersive technology's impact in resource-poor regions.
In rural India, VR labs let students conduct scientific experiments virtually despite lacking physical labs and equipment.
Sarita Patel, a technology education advocate in Rajasthan, India, says VR lets students do physics and chemistry experiments they could not otherwise witness.
On November 19, 2023, Ghanaian teacher Kofi Annan's class virtually visited the Great Barrier Reef using VR to teach conservation.
Elizabeth Jensen, an American educator and tech innovator, said on December 5, 2023, that students who struggle with conventional teaching are thriving with personalized VR/AR.
The "EdTech Innovate" program launched in Egypt on September 25, 2023, using virtual labs and AR-powered textbooks for science and mathematics as part of nationwide educational reform.
Program director Hassan Abdel Fattah called investment in VR and AR "not a luxury" but a stride towards democratizing education.
On October 30, 2023, Colombia's government and NPO Tech4Hope launched a professional development program training educators in immersive technologies.
Maria Consuelo, a teacher from Bogotá, said she was initially skeptical but now finds the tools indispensable after the training.
